Who are the Governors and what do they do?
Who are the Governors?
Governors are volunteers who work in partnership with their school headteacher to ensure that children receive the best education possible. Governors represent the largest volunteer group in the UK and are selected from a variety of backgrounds to reflect the many interest groups within our schools.
The Governing Body has the following core strategic functions:
Every school has a Governing Body, which sets the strategic framework for the school in partnership with the Headteacher. The governing body should have a strong focus on three core strategic functions:
Establishing the strategic direction, by:
Ensuring accountability, by:
Ensuring financial probity, by:
The Governing Body works with the Headteacher who is responsible for the day-to-day running of the school, including the management of the staff. Governors work with the Headteacher to:
Our role as governors is to support our school, acting as 'ambassadors', mediators and 'critical friends'.
If you have any questions or feel you could become a Governor, please contact the Clerk to Governors on 01474 569859.

Careers Week 2025
Shaping Our Future: A Vibrant Recap of Careers Week at Singlewell Primary School
Last week we had an exciting Careers Week that took place at Singlewell Primary School, where our pupils embarked on an inspiring journey exploring various professions and envisioning their future careers. Throughout the week, students had the opportunity to engage with professionals from diverse fields, gaining insights and sparking their imaginations about the endless possibilities that lie ahead.
Careers Week was a huge success, filled with inspiration, curiosity, and excitement! Throughout the week, students had the chance to hear from a wide range of guest speakers including midwives, firemen, sports presenters, game programmers, Arctic explorers, and many more fascinating professionals. A highlight was the Careers Fair for Years 2 to 6, where students asked thoughtful questions to experts in diverse roles such as a photographer, hairdresser, global procurement manager, financial advisor, midwife, head nurse, and teacher. It was a fantastic opportunity for children to explore future possibilities and dream big!
We would also like to say a big thank you to all the parents and carers who supported our Careers Week dress-up day. Your creativity and effort in helping the children come dressed as their future selves truly brought the day to life. Seeing the excitement and pride on the children’s faces made it all the more special, and it's these moments that help make events like this both memorable and meaningful. Another HUGE thank you to all of our guests, without you our careers week would not have been as successful for all our pupils.
Everyone's continued support plays a huge part in supporting us to enrich your children's school experience— so thank you!
Pupil Development Lead

Personal Development
At Singlewell, our curriculum provides for learners' broader development. As well as academic development, it is essential that children are given pathways, through the curriculum and beyond, for personal development. We have carefully planned our wider experiences to provide plentiful opportunities to enable our children to discover their interests and talents while teaching them how to engage with society. We want our children to develop their resilience, confidence and independence and leave Primary School feeling empowered to achieve their goals and ambitions.
Our aim is to teach children how to navigate through life safely, happily and healthily (physically and mentally). Children are growing up in a world that is constantly changing and it is the duty of all the staff at Singlewell, in partnership with the parents, to teach the children transferable life skills. We teach children about the world around them, relationships, emotions, and health, as well as transferable skills to help with life.

Reception 2027 – Open Mornings
We would be delighted to welcome prospective parents and carers to visit Singlewell Primary School ahead of their child starting Reception in September 2027.
For children starting Reception in September 2027, their date of birth will normally fall between 1 September 2022 and 31 August 2023.
Our Open Mornings will take place on the following dates, with tours available at 9:30am and 10:30am:
Wednesday 30 September 2026
Wednesday 14 October 2026
Wednesday 21 October 2026
Wednesday 18 November 2026
Wednesday 25 November 2026
Wednesday 6 January 2027
Saturday Coffee Morning
We will also be holding an informal Coffee Morning on Saturday 10 October 2026, from 10:00am to 12:00pm.
This is another opportunity to visit the school, meet members of staff and find out more about life at Singlewell Primary School.
Book your visit
Places must be booked in advance. Please use our online booking form to select the date and time you would like to attend.
To help us manage numbers, please book a maximum of two adults per family. Where possible, we kindly ask that children do not attend so that parents and carers can get the most from the visit. We appreciate that this may not always be possible.
Book your Reception 2027 visit
If you have any questions, please contact the School Office on 01474 569859.
Singlewell Primary School - Admission Arrangements
Singlewell Primary School is a community school and Kent County Council (KCC) is the admission authority.
The school's Published Admission Number (PAN) is 60, meaning that up to 60 children are normally admitted into Reception each year.
Applications are made through Kent County Council's (KCC) Primary Admissions process.
Applications open on Friday 6 November 2026 and close on Friday 15 January 2027.
National Offer Day is Friday 16 April 2027.
Parents and carers can find further information and apply online through the KCC Primary School Places website.
Children with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) that names Singlewell Primary School will be admitted before the oversubscription criteria are applied.
If there are more applications than places available, KCC applies its published admissions criteria. In summary, priority is given in the following order:
Full details, including definitions, tie-break arrangements, waiting lists and appeals, can be found in Kent County Council's Admissions Criteria for 2027/28.
For further information, please contact the School Office on 01474 569859 or Kent County Council Primary Admissions on 03000 412121.

pageCache.text:
A Fire Engine visits Singlewell
A fire engine visited our Year 2 pupils as part of their learning about the Great Fire of London. The children were excited to meet real firefighters and explore the equipment used to tackle modern-day fires. The visit helped them compare past and present firefighting methods, deepening their understanding of how technology and safety have evolved since 1666. The hands-on experience brought their history topic to life, sparked thoughtful questions and supported rich discussion back in the classroom.
It was particularly exciting when they got to spray the powerful hose down the school drive, under the careful supervision of the Firefighter!

Family Learning Courses
Free face-to-face Family Learning Courses at Singlewell Primary School
After the success of our first Family Learning course held at Singlewell we are pleased to be holding two more Family Learning courses this year.
In Term 4 we will be holding a Family First Aid Course. It will be held across three Friday mornings and you must be available to attend all of these sessions. The course is run by Kent Family Learning, a part of Kent Adult Education. It will require practical participation. Unfortunately, due to it's practical nature, pre-school age children and babies are not able to attend.
It will be held in our school sports hall with refreshments provided. Come along to expand your knowledge and learn some new skills in a friendly environment.
Open to all parents, carers and family members. Please speak to, or email, Mrs Hazeldene to confirm your attendance.
'Stepping Up' into Secondary School
Later in Term 5 we will be holding a workshop, specifically aimed at our Year 6 parents, to support their understanding around the expectations of Secondary School life and how to support their child through this transition.
The course is run by Kent Family Learning, a part of Kent Adult Education.
It will be held in our school sports hall with refreshments provided.
Open to all parents, carers and family members of Year 6 pupils. Please speak to, or email, Mrs Hazeldene to confirm your attendance.
Exploring Behaviour Strategies
On Monday 10th February 2025 we had our first Family Learning course held at Singlewell Primary School. A group of parents and carers came together with Carrie-Ann, our Family Learning Providor and Mrs Hazeldene, our school SENCO to develop their understanding of behaviour and to learn behaviour strategies to add to their parent toolkit.
Hear from our parents and carers who were in attendance:
" A very good session with lots of information."
"Great detailed explanations of child behaviours. I hope to attend more courses like this."
"I found today's course quite good as both the SENCo and course teacher had lots of good ideas, resources and approaches to consider trying when facing challenging behaviours from my child. I have learnt about recognising emotional cues and how to support them to regulate. "
"This workshop was very informative. The Tutor was very engaging."
"Helpful tips to try at home."

Science Week 2026
Primary schools celebrate Science Week to inspire curiosity, encourage a love of learning, and help children see how science connects to the world around them. It gives pupils the chance to explore ideas in a fun, hands-on way that goes beyond the usual classroom routine. During the week, we took part in exciting activities like DIY rocket launches, where we learned about forces and motion, and bubble making, which helped us explore shapes and surface tension & a spectacular visit from the Wonderdome helping us to explore the phenomenon that is space! We also joined interactive online workshops that introduced us to real scientists and fascinating experiments. These experiences made science feel exciting and accessible, helping us build confidence, creativity, and a deeper curiosity in how things work.
